newsitem.title: USA: NYS MTA TO PULL REFUNDING PART OF BIG BOND SALE.
newsitem.headline: NYS MTA TO PULL REFUNDING PART OF BIG BOND SALE.

text.p: The Metropolitan Transporation Authority of the State of New York, finding the recent rise in interest rates made a refunding too costly, plans to pull a $215 million offering, underwriter Smith Barney said Monday.
However, the Authority still expects to sell this week about $446 million of new money bonds through negotiation, an official with the brokerage house added.
"Due to market conditions, the refunding portion of the loan will not be coming this week," said an official with the underwriter, who declined to be named.
A spokesman for the Metropolitan Transportation Authority was not immediately available to comment.

While there has been speculation that the roughly 40-basis point rise in Treasury bond yields since mid-July might cause more issuers to scale back their offerings, especially refundings, Portland, Ore., decided to competitively sell on Tuesday at 1300 EDT/1000 PDT/1700 GMT just over $267 million of refunding sewer system bonds.
